notes: Uses system_selector_scenarios.Namespace with two disposable root user namespace layers and fixture-owned preinstall.d configuration. No non-root polkit or multiuser claim.
Only public .preinstall definitions, CLI queries and fixture payloads at publicly returned deployment locations are inspected. No installed repository backend paths are constructed.
The preinstall manual in this checkout is doc/flatpak-preinstall.xml. Install=false explicitly removes the app; the runtime remains designated for installation.

History uses an actual systemd-journald process and journalctl --sync within one guarded namespace invocation. Each nested CLI argv, exit status, stdout and stderr is retained as JSON lines in outer command evidence. User history refers to namespace root's per-user installation, not an ordinary user's authorization behavior. Lifecycle checks require ordered installation/update/removal concepts for controlled refs, accepting noun/verb aliases and an optional deployment prefix. Unknown auxiliary labels and repeated events do not satisfy missing lifecycle steps and do not impose fixed record counts. The documented installation column must identify the selected store; auxiliary records may identify temporary repository paths. Pure helper controls accept extra auxiliary records and reject wrong selectors, missing steps, wrong order and swapped columns.

Repair adds a third disposable user namespace mapping actual UID/GID 1000 to enclosing namespace UID/GID 0. Both callers query the same populated default system installation without installation/config redirects. Exact ref/commit checks bracket authorized root repair, which may rebuild filesystem objects. Device/inode identities at public installation/deployment paths are captured after root repair and must match across the non-root namespace and its read-only repair. The inherited host root remains read-only and no host bus is present. Coverage is limited to actual non-root refusal to mutate, including automatic dry-run; repository-object recovery and dry-run inconsistency detection remain unmapped.

Preinstall --system receives no option assertion because ignoring it still selects the default system installation. No preinstall --no-pull assertion is claimed: the attempted cached setup returned Nothing to do even without that flag. Download-only is verified by empty installed queries and subsequent ordinary offline installation of its downloaded content.

behaviors.description: Download vendor refs without deployment, then verify cached content through ordinary offline installation.
behaviors.preconditions: Fresh stores, vendor app/runtime definitions and local fixture origin.
behaviors.expected: Preinstall download-only leaves installed list empty; ordinary install --no-pull then deploys exact cached commits after origin URL becomes unavailable.

behaviors.description: Query real journal records from controlled install/update/uninstall operations.
behaviors.preconditions: Real systemd-journald in one disposable namespace invocation, private volatile journal and sockets; root's per-user installation is the user subject.
behaviors.expected: Required lifecycle events appear in chronological order with correct ref and installation fields, allowing auxiliary records; reverse exactly reverses observed forward rows and disjoint time ranges are empty.

behaviors.description: Synchronize vendor definitions through the public transaction API.
behaviors.preconditions: Fresh system installation with fixture remote and app/runtime preinstall definitions.
behaviors.expected: Ready operations are exactly two installs followed by one app uninstall after configuration changes; public installed queries match both results.

behaviors.description: Contrast successful namespace-root repair with actual non-root denial for the same isolated installation.
behaviors.preconditions: Populated default system store inherited by a third disposable namespace with actual UID/GID 1000; same public paths and post-root-repair device/inode identities, caller-owned writable base, no installation/config redirects or host bus.
behaviors.expected: Root repair succeeds without a dry-run warning and retains app/runtime refs and commits; UID 1000 repair refuses mutation and preserves the post-root-repair public filesystem identities and commits.

behaviors.description: Synchronize default vendor definitions through install, removal and re-addition.
behaviors.preconditions: Fresh private stores and one documented .preinstall file naming the app and runtime.
behaviors.expected: Default synchronization installs both refs; Install=false removes only the app; restoring Install=true reinstalls it.

behaviors.description: Contrast manual-uninstall opt-out with a fresh named installation using identical definitions.
behaviors.preconditions: App and runtime successfully preinstalled, then app manually uninstalled from default.
behaviors.expected: Named preinstall installs the app; default preinstall leaves it absent and preserves the runtime.

behaviors.description: Enumerate configured installation paths and compare generated system/user environments.
behaviors.preconditions: Private default, named and root-user installation locations.
behaviors.expected: Exact two-member system path set; both exports in generated data paths; system-only removes precisely user exports.

mappings.rationale: Paired download/deploy phases observe no deployments followed by exact cached deployments while the origin is unavailable.

surface_assertions.rationale: Successful download leaves the fresh installed set empty but supplies content for subsequent ordinary offline installation.

mappings.rationale: A private real journal records actual user install, update and removal calls; history must contain those semantic lifecycle steps in order for the required refs and user installation. Auxiliary labels/counts are unrestricted. Wrong-source histories and omitted lifecycle steps are rejected by controls.

surface_assertions.rationale: User lifecycle rows identify the user installation, with runtime/app installs followed by app update and removal; other configured installation IDs are rejected.
Default runtime/app installation events identify system in the documented installation column; named/user source IDs are rejected.
Named runtime/app installs and app update identify alt in the installation column; default/user source IDs are rejected.
Output equals the exact reverse of actual forward user rows, including whatever auxiliary events the target emits.
A future lower bound excludes all records present in the control query.
A past upper bound excludes all records present in the control query.

Requested installation/ref/change order yields three fields with the selected installation ID, exact fixture ref and a recognized lifecycle concept for each required event. Swapped-column control fails.

mappings.rationale: CALL_API sync adds exact typed ready operations for both installation and vendor app removal; running each changes public installed sets and preserves other stores.

Actual UID/EUID 1000 is denied mutation after root repair succeeds without a dry-run warning. Exact seeded refs/commits are checked before and after authorized root repair. Its resulting public system/deployment identities establish the baseline checked across the non-root namespace and read-only repair, without redirects. The base remains caller-owned and writable. No polkit or multiuser claim.
No action flags: exact public ref sets and commits show installation, vendor removal, and successful re-addition.
An actionable unchanged definition installs in fresh alt but does not undo manual default uninstall.

surface_assertions.rationale: User sync installs the app in the previously empty user store while default remains opted out and alt stays installed.
Named sync deploys the app in fresh alt while the manually removed default copy stays absent.

mappings.rationale: Exact configured path enumeration and paired generated environments establish user exclusion; supplied sentinel data directory survives amendment with all installation exports added.

surface_assertions.rationale: Output is exactly the two configured system paths, with no duplicates or user path.
Parsed XDG_DATA_DIRS contains exports for both systems and the user installation.
Paired output excludes the user export path and retains every other path in order.
